instantiated_cells.justification: The statute requires the principal (not the lobbyist) to file periodic expense statements, indicating there is no separate lobbyist-filed periodic spending report requirement.
Because the required periodic spending report is filed by principals rather than lobbyists, there is no lobbyist spending report cadence that includes an annual filing.
The only periodic spending report described is the principal’s semiannual expense statement, not a lobbyist monthly spending report.
The statute sets semiannual principal filings and does not create any quarterly lobbyist-filed spending report.
Although filings are due July 31 and Jan. 31, they are required of principals, so the lobbyist is not the named filer of a semiannual spending report.
No triannual spending report is required of lobbyists; the only periodic statement described is the principal’s expense statement.
The statute does not establish any other lobbyist-filed periodic spending report cadence because the periodic report obligation is imposed on principals.
Wisconsin law requires principals to file semiannual expense statements, but does not require lobbyists to file a periodic spending report, so the lobbyist spending report cadence is none.
Total lobbying expenditures are reported in the principal’s expense statement, not in any lobbyist-filed spending report, so the lobbyist report does not include total expenditures.
Compensation to lobbyists is included in the principal’s aggregate reported expenditures, but the statute does not require a lobbyist-filed spending report disclosing compensation.
The reporting obligation is imposed on principals and does not require lobbyists to file a spending report breaking compensation down by payer.
Indirect costs are addressed in the principal’s expense statement, but there is no lobbyist-filed periodic spending report requiring disclosure of such costs.
While certain reimbursements may be reported by principals, the statute does not create a lobbyist-filed spending report that includes gifts, entertainment, transportation, or lodging.
The statute requires principals to file an expense statement and does not require lobbyists to file an itemized expenses report.
Because there is no separate lobbyist-filed spending report, the law does not require lobbyists to use an itemized spending-report format.

Expense categorization requirements apply to the principal’s expense statement rather than any lobbyist-filed spending report, so lobbyists are not required to categorize expenses in a separate report.

Identification of legislative proposals/topics is a principal reporting obligation, not a lobbyist spending report requirement, so lobbyists are not required to include bill/action identifiers in a spending report.
The requirement to report each legislative proposal or rule number is imposed on principals, and the statute does not require lobbyists to file a spending report listing specific bill numbers.
General topics/issues must be reported by principals when not tied to a numbered proposal, but the law does not require lobbyists to file their own spending report including general issues.
Subject-matter/topic reporting is required of principals and is not part of any lobbyist-filed periodic spending report.

The principal must describe topics sufficiently to identify whether attempting to influence legislative or administrative action, but no lobbyist spending report is required and no position-on-bill disclosure by lobbyists is mandated.
The statute requires principals to estimate time proportion by proposal/topic, not lobbyists to report expenditures per issue in a lobbyist spending report.
The daily time record of meetings and activities is part of the principal’s expense statement requirements and does not impose a lobbyist spending report requirement to disclose contacts made.
Lobbyists provide information on a license application, but the statute does not require lobbyists to file periodic spending reports that include their contact information.
Authorization filings identify the principal-lobbyist relationship, but the law does not require lobbyists to file a periodic spending report listing principals represented.
Principal name and business address are required in the principal’s registration statement, not in any lobbyist-filed periodic spending report.

Descriptions of the principal’s business activity or purposes are part of the principal’s registration filing, and there is no lobbyist spending report requiring disclosure of the principal’s business nature.
The reporting duty applies to registered principals on fixed dates and the statute does not impose any lobbyist-filed periodic spending report (including a no-activity report) requirement.
Because Wisconsin does not require lobbyists to file a periodic spending report, it does not define the report’s scope to include household members of officials.
